diagnostic_audit_name: Empirical Audit of Metric Alignment & Bilateral Fusion

audit_summary.flaw_1_data_snooping: The previously reported 638.2 hits were obtained via validation-target snooping during checkpoint selection. Under strict out-of-fold partitioning, Bi-MeF on compact models achieves ~538 hits.
audit_summary.flaw_2_architecture_suboptimality: On compact representations, Ablation C (bilateral cross-terms W_c2s, W_s2c without gating) yields 555 hits, outperforming the full gated model (538 hits) by 17 hits, proving the 4-way router overfits.
audit_summary.flaw_3_weak_backbone_artifact: The apparent gain of Cosine PoE (from 311 to 522 hits on compact models) is an artifact of uncalibrated embedding norms in under-trained models, where cosine normalization acts as an ad-hoc popularity regularizer.
audit_summary.decisive_strong_backbone_result: On properly trained high-capacity backbones (SASRec alone = 741-765 hits, Static Dot PoE = 765-772 hits), Cosine PoE drops to 740 hits (-25 hits vs Dot PoE), Ablation C yields 748 hits (-17 hits), and Full Bi-MeF yields 774 hits (+9 hits, strictly within the MDE noise floor of 19.8-28.6 hits, p = 0.38).

scientific_conclusion: Metric alignment and bilateral cross-projections merely compensate for under-trained or poorly calibrated representations in weak backbones. When evaluated on state-of-the-art sequential backbones, cosine scoring strips true popularity priors (-25 hits), and learned dynamic fusion is statistically equivalent to static 50/50 PoE.
